title: Introducing the Leap Year Code Challenge
summary: Sets out the leap year rules, shows a flowchart of the decision order, and explains the exact output strings the next exercise expects.

concepts.heading: Leap year rules
points: A year divisible by 4 is a leap year.
Exception: a year also divisible by 100 is not a leap year.
Exception to the exception: a year also divisible by 400 is a leap year.
Example: 2000 divides by 4, by 100 and by 400, so it is a leap year. 1900 divides by 4 and 100 but not 400, so it is not.
Background: leap years compensate for the mismatch between the calendar and the Earth's orbit; the exercise links an explainer video and a reference site that steps through the rules.

concepts.heading: Flowchart approach
points: Draw the logic as a flowchart (draw.io) before coding.
Step 1: divisible by 4? If no, not a leap year.
Step 2: divisible by 100? If no, leap year.
Step 3: divisible by 400? If yes, leap year; if no, not a leap year.
Each decision diamond maps to an if statement, so the chart can be translated straight into code.

task.name: Leap Year challenge
task.starting_point: Exercise page with a function to write that receives a year.
task.goal: Return the exact string "Leap year." or "Not leap year." for the given year.
steps: Write the logic using the modulo operator (year % 4 === 0 and so on) inside if/else.
Match the output text exactly, including capital letter, space and full stop, or the tests fail.
task.expected_result: 2000 gives "Leap year."; 1900 and 2023 give "Not leap year."
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.06 - Leap Year Challenge Exercise/script.js

pitfalls: Checking 100 before 4, or forgetting the 400 exception.
Using = instead of === in the comparisons.
